content_preview.title: Mistral Launches Voxtral 3 With Four Speech Models and a LiveKit-Based Voice Agent SDK, Pricing Voice Agents From $0.04 per Minute
content_preview.summary: Mistral AI's Voxtral 3 post lists three transcription models, a text-to-speech model at $13 per 1M characters and a voice agent SDK built on LiveKit; benchmark claims are Mistral's own.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Mistral AI has introduced Voxtral 3, which it describes in a [post on its website](https://mistral.ai/news/voxtral-3/) as "a new family of state-of-the-art speech-to-text and text-to-speech models, alongside a voice agent SDK that brings listening, thinking, tool calling, and speaking into a single real-time streaming pipeline." The post, published October 22 according to the page's publication metadata, says the models are available through the Mistral API.

editor_notes.content_quality: Briefing of 651 words (range 300-800) with Overview, What We Know, Benchmarks and Caveats, What We Don't Know and Context sections. Clear, structured, appropriate technical depth; vendor claims are consistently attributed to Mistral.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both snapshots read from disk (source-0.html.gz mistral.ai/news/voxtral-3/, source-1.html.gz techcrunch.com March 26 piece), raw HTML text, then live re-fetched with WebFetch (live results agreed with snapshots). No suspicious_patterns in either manifest entry. Both hosts are on config/source_allowlist.txt (techcrunch.com line 99, mistral.ai line 2837). SOURCE 0 (Mistral, vendor first-party, the only source for Voxtral 3): (1) Date: JSON-LD datePublished and dateModified are 2026-10-22T09:00:00+02:00, confirming 'October 22' (WebFetch's text rendering shows no date; the page metadata is authoritative). (2) Opening quote 'a new family of state-of-the-art speech-to-text and text-to-speech models, alongside a voice agent SDK that brings listening, thinking, tool calling, and speaking into a single real-time streaming pipeline' is verbatim. (3) Pricing table: Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3 (batch) $0.0035/min, Mini Transcribe Realtime 3 $0.008/min, Small Transcribe 3 $0.0040/min, TTS $13/1M chars, 'Voice agent API with Mistral Small 4 for reasoning' 0.04$/min, 'Voice agent API with larger model' 0.08$/min: all match. Model count: the post lists three transcription models plus Voxtral Mini TTS 3, i.e. four priced models, so 'four speech models' in the title is consistent with the post's pricing table; the post itself says 'family' without a numeric count. Note the post names the realtime model 'Voxtral Realtime Transcribe 3' in one body paragraph and 'Voxtral Mini Transcribe Realtime 3' in the SDK paragraph, pricing table and product card; the article uses the latter, which is the priced name. (4) Mini is 4B parameters at $0.0035/min: 'The Mini variant is 4B parameters ... at a price of $0.0035/min' confirmed. Small: 'over 50 languages', diarization, context biasing confirmed. (5) Language coverage for realtime: body 'sub-500ms latency in over 35 languages' and product card 'sub-500ms latency across 40+ languages' both present; the article reports both and attributes them correctly (the FLEURS realtime chart lists 35 languages). TTS '35+ languages and 50+ dialects' confirmed. (6) LiveKit: 'a voice agent SDK, built on LiveKit' confirmed; pipeline description, 'a general model-like Mistral Small-reasons and calls tools' (quote reproduced with the link text 'Mistral Small' as in the post), under one second per turn, barge-in, SIP and WebRTC all confirmed. The $0.04/min price is for the voice agent API with Mistral Small 4 for reasoning, and $0.08/min with a larger model, as the article says. (7) Pro Voice reproduces 'a speaker's distinctive character, emotional range, and speaking style' from 'just 30 minutes of audio': confirmed. (8) Deployment quote 'hosted through our European, US, and global endpoints' verbatim; 'talk to our team' for on-premises/private cloud confirmed. (9) Benchmarks: 'It outperforms Whisper, Scribe v2 and Gemini 3.5 Transcribe' (Small) verbatim; 'Voxtral TTS costs less to run than comparable models from OpenAI TTS-1, Deepgram, ElevenLabs Flash and Gemini Flash' verbatim. Four TTS chart captions: Voice Code Bench (attributed to BeSimple AI, judge gemini-3.8-flash) and three captioned 'Internal eval' (pronunciation, multilingual, expressive English), each with 'judge gemini-3.8-flash; prices from vendor pricing pages; generated 2026-10-20'. The article's statement that the judge model was gemini-3.8-flash and that several charts are labeled 'Internal eval' is exact; the article labels all as Mistral's own. (10) Absence verified by raw HTML search: no occurrence of 'open weight', 'open-source', 'Apache', 'license/licence', 'weights'; the only 'Hugging Face' string is the organization JSON-LD sameAs link to huggingface.co/mistralai, not a model release. The article's claim that the post does not describe a weights release or license is correct. SOURCE 1 (TechCrunch, independent but dated 2026-03-26T11:30:00+00:00 per JSON-LD): describes 'a new open source text-to-speech model' (verbatim, supports nine languages, matching 'nine languages'). Pierre Stock is 'VP of science operations at Mistral AI'; the quote 'We plan to have an end-to-end platform that can handle multimodal streams of input, including audio, text, and image and output as well' is verbatim, is a complete sentence followed by a further sentence in the original (the article ends the quote at the period, acceptable), is attributed to Stock via 'told TechCrunch' (he spoke in a phone interview per the piece) and dated March correctly. The TechCrunch piece does not mention Voxtral 3; the article states Voxtral 3 post 'does not reference Stock's remark' (true, the post contains no Stock remark). INDEPENDENCE: only one of two sources is independent of the subject, and it does not cover Voxtral 3; every Voxtral 3 fact rests solely on Mistral's own post. The article states this ('No independent evaluation of Voxtral 3 appears in the sources reviewed'). Briefing category carries no independence requirement. INTERNAL LINK: /article/2026-03/27-mistral-releases-voxtral-tts-a-4-billion-parameter-open-weight-text-to-speech-model-that-rivals-elevenlabs resolves to an existing published article (src/content/articles/2026-03/27-...md), described accurately as the Herald's earlier Voxtral TTS coverage. No orphan URLs: body URLs are the two sources plus that internal link.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All numbers, names, dates, quotes and attributions checked individually against raw source text; no discrepancies. Headline 'four speech models' = three transcription + one TTS, consistent with the post's pricing table; headline LiveKit and $0.04/min claims supported (the $0.04 is conditional on Mistral Small 4 reasoning, as the article states in the body).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral. Vendor claims attributed ('Mistral says'), benchmarks explicitly labeled as Mistral's own, absence of independent evaluation and of open-weights information disclosed. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: New story. The only related Herald article is the March Voxtral TTS piece, linked as prior coverage; no Voxtral 3 coverage exists in 2026-10.
concerns: Single-source for all Voxtral 3 facts (vendor first-party); the independent source predates the release and does not cover Voxtral 3. The article discloses this.
The post uses two names for the realtime model; the article uses the priced name.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed vendor-release Briefing with careful caveats on benchmarks, language-count discrepancy and open-weights absence. Approved with no corrections. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate release coverage of a voice-agent SDK and pricing for a defined developer audience
